PullRequest.Title: chat: keep model picker selection motion consistent
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #347188

Changing a model's effort, context, or speed in the model picker details sometimes slid the selection and sometimes snapped it, depending on the setting and direction. Saving a choice refreshes the details card, and that refresh rebuilt the segmented controls while the selection was still moving.

The card now waits for the selection to settle before it rebuilds, and combines any refreshes that arrive in the meantime. Values still apply right away. With reduced motion on there is no slide, so nothing waits. While a choice is still saving, the card keeps showing it, so a refresh can't put back an older value. If the settings or their choices change, for example a model with different effort levels, the card rebuilds right away instead of waiting.

### Before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b027714-bcc0-49bc-a965-8930f353da57

### After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/349da338-9e27-4039-8512-6e4d33360e58

Both clips show GPT-6.1 Sol in the Agents window, changing effort, context, and speed in both directions.

### How to test

1. Open the model picker and open the details for a model with effort, context, and speed options, such as GPT-6.1 Sol.
2. Change each setting back and forth. The selection should slide every time, in both directions.
3. Set `workbench.reduceMotion` to `on` and repeat. Changes should apply instantly without sliding.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/radio/radio.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerCard.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerTabbedWidget.test.ts --grep 'Radio|ModelCard|TabbedModelPicker'`: 263 passing
- The same command with `--force-prefers-reduced-motion`: 263 passing
- Each new regression test fails without its fix.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run eslint` on the five changed files: passed

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh a model Details card while an effort/context/speed selection indicator is moving
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each refresh synchronously reads the two configuration bindings and inspects at most the card's three Radio controls. If a 160 ms selection transition is active, the changed code defers the DOM rebuild until it settles; the already-rendered control remains interactive, and repeated refreshes are off the rebuild critical path because they are coalesced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of controls on one details card (effort, context, speed; effectively at most three) and refresh events during one 160 ms transition. Refreshes during that interval collapse to one deferred rebuild.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single `_renderPending` flag permits one deferred render waiter per card. Each waiter observes the bounded control set with `Promise.all`; no unbounded task or animation concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model cards are cached per picker/model until the popup hides. `_renderedBindings` is a per-card snapshot; configuration values/schema are served from the existing in-memory model configuration store after its first read. Cold construction already had to read the same configuration to render controls; the added binding snapshot shifts/adds bounded synchronous reads but does not add a new cold boundary. There is no negative-cache retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed getters, coalescing flag, 160 ms CSS transition, card cache, and bounded three-control call path are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact DOM rebuild cost varies with model metadata and messages, but the diff reduces repeated rebuilds during a transition and adds only bounded binding/animation inspection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added synchronous work is constant and small, while the changed scheduling coalesces refresh-driven DOM reconstruction rather than multiplying it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose an effort or context configuration value from the open model Details card
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The radio selection updates immediately, then the existing per-model save must finish; selection acceptance also waits for the bounded selection transition. Configuration-change refreshes may arrive during the save/animation and are now combined into one rebuild. The pending-edit overlay is consulted only by synchronous renders before the save completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the editor-scoped configuration bucket through `IStorageService` and update/remove/add the language-model provider settings group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `setModelConfiguration` call per distinct user choice, serialized per model; a real change performs the existing scoped storage write and settings-group update (potentially across existing configuration-only groups).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, `_setValues` called the same `setModelConfigValues` once per choice and awaited the same persistence path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The save is awaited before selection acceptance and final rebuild, as it was before the diff. The optimistic overlay changes what interim renders read but does not add another persistence call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User choices queued for one model. Saves remain serialized by `SequencerByKey`; realistic pending-edit cardinality is the number of clicks made before prior persistence completes, and ordinary completion removes each entry in `finally`.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One persistence operation runs at a time per model/configuration scope; later choices queue. The changed Set does not increase save concurrency, and one card can have only one deferred render waiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration reads use the editor-scoped in-memory snapshot after the first read. Pending optimistic edits are overlaid in insertion order and are removed on success or failure. Empty/failure states do not become cached retries; card disposal does not prevent the save's existing promise chain from settling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed `_saveValues` is a one-for-one wrapper around the prior call, and the unchanged sequencer and persistence implementations establish cardinality and serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider settings persistence duration and rapid-click frequency vary, but the diff neither increases boundary-call count nor aggregate concurrency. Overlay copy cost grows with pending clicks, which are already retained by the serialized promise queue and are normally very small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Boundary count and critical-path waits are unchanged; refresh coalescing reduces DOM churn, and pending entries have explicit success/failure cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive model metadata, schema, policy, pin, or configuration updates while a selection is moving
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `ModelCard.update` or `refresh` compares the rendered effort/context keys and enum choices. If those bindings changed, it rebuilds immediately; otherwise it waits for the active transition and combines intervening updates. This path is synchronous UI work with no subprocess, IPC, database, network, or direct filesystem operation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two configuration groups and the enum lengths for one displayed model; equality work is linear only in those bounded choice arrays, not in the full model list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One update executes synchronously and at most one deferred rebuild remains pending. Model-list refresh work outside the card is pre-existing and is not multiplied by this change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The comparison uses the current schema/configuration snapshot and the last rendered bindings. Warm reads are in-memory; changed choices bypass the deferred path immediately. No new long-lived cache keys or invalidation responsibility is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the binding extraction and equality checks are explicit, and the caller routes only the current details card through this method.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extensions can expose varying enum lengths, but model configuration controls are small segmented-choice sets; no collection-wide or boundary-scaled work was introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new comparison is bounded to one visible card and prevents unnecessary immediate reconstruction when the controls still fit.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and their relevant callers, animation lifecycle, configuration cache, persistence path, and disposal behavior. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found, and the PR did not provide sufficient evidence of a shipped performance-regression fix to record.
